defects.justification: http.ListenAndServe runs a default http.Server with no read-header/read/write/idle timeouts, so slow or stalled clients can tie up connections and long export queries indefinitely.

The CSV export writes customer_name (and status) verbatim with no neutralisation of leading =, +, -, @, so a customer-controlled name becomes a spreadsheet formula when an admin opens the export (the README admits this rather than fixing it).

On a scan, marshal or rows error mid-export the JSON writer just logs, breaks and still writes the closing `]` with a 200 status, so the client receives a well-formed but silently truncated export (same pattern in writeOrdersCSV at line 341-344).
The return values of cw.Write are ignored and cw.Error() is never checked after cw.Flush(), so CSV write failures are lost.
The API-key middleware has no rate limiting or lockout on failed attempts, so the admin endpoints can be brute-forced or used to hammer the database with unlimited unauthenticated lookups.
writeJSON ignores the error returned by json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v).
